title: CRLR/181/2011 of KAPU Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME,SECRETARIAT COMPLEX

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 181 of 2011
Kapu ...Revisionist
Versus

State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt for the revisionist.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to the
followings:-
(i) Judgment and order dated 21.11.2008,
passed in Criminal Case No. 72 of 2007,
State Vs. Kapu, by the court of Judicial
Magistrate, Uttarkashi ("the case"). By it, the
revisionist has been convicted under
Sections 60 (1) and 60 (2) of the U.P. Excise
Act, 1910, (the Act"). The revisionist has
been sentenced to imprisonment till rising of
the court with a fine of Rs.5,000/- under
Section 60 (1) of the Act. It has further been
directed that in default of payment of fine
the revisionist shall undergo simple
imprisonment for a further period of three
months. The revisionist has also been

2
sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment
for a period of one year with a fine of
Rs.7000/- under Section 60 (2) of the Act. In
default of payment of fine to undergo simple
imprisonment for a further period of four
months; and
(ii) Judgment and order dated 21.07.2011,
passed in Criminal Appeal No. 40 of 2008,
Kapu Vs. State and another, by the court of
Sessions Judge, Uttarkashi ("the appeal").
By it, the impugned judgment and order
dated 21.11.2008 has been confirmed and
appeal dismissed.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the case, on 18.01.2007, when the
police were on patrolling duty, they spotted the revisionist
manufacturing illicit liquor. Apart from the substance, by
which the liquor is made, it is the case that 10 litres liquor
and other equipments were recovered. After investigation,
the matter was placed before the court. Cognizance was
taken. On 13.01.2007, charges under Section 60 (1) of the
Act and Section 60 (2) of the Act were framed.

3
4. In order to prove its case, the prosecution
examined two witnesses, namely, PW1 Devesh Tripathi and
PW2 Dinesh Singh Rawat.
5. The revisionist was examined under Section 313
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. According to him,
he has been falsely implicated.
6. After hearing the parties, by the impugned
judgments and orders, the revisionist has been convicted
and sentenced, as stated hereinbefore. The judgment passed
in the case was unsuccessfully challenged in appeal. Hence,
the revision.
7. Learned counsel for the revisionist would raise
only one question. According to him, either the revisionist
may be released on probation or the amount of fine may be
enhanced, but he may not now be sentenced to
imprisonment. It is argued that the revisionist is a very poor
person. He is a snake charmer and he did not commit any
offence in the past or after this incident. It is also submitted
that the revisionist has been in custody for about 20 days.
8. Learned State counsel would admit that the
revisionist has been in custody in this case for 20 days.
9. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court
is of the view that the interest of justice would be better

4
served if the sentence is modified and the revisionist instead
of imprisonment may be punished with fine only.
10. The conviction of the revisionist under Section 60
(1) of the Act remains unaltered. However, the sentence
under Section 60 (2) of the Act, is modified to the extent that
the revisionist is sentenced to a period which he had already
undergone with a fine of Rs. 10,000/- .
11. The revision is partly allowed.
12. The impugned judgments and orders are modified
to the extent, as indicated above.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 22.09.2022
Jitendra
